title: Three equivalent forms, the density factor $\rho_K$, and Class-A discipline status
html:
Remark. Three equivalent forms, the density factor \rho_K, and Class-A discipline status

Three equivalent forms

The same observable \mathfrak{m}(K) admits three rewritings. Each exposes different structure:

Form Inputs Status
(GB-NF) \mathfrak{m} = m_e \cdot \rho_K \cdot \lvert\!\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\mathcal{B}_K)\bigr)\!\rvert m_e, \mathcal{B}_K, q_0, \rho_K algebraic
(constituent) \mathfrak{m} = Z m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z m_e + \alpha \sum_i \ln\lvert\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}}\rvert m_e, \mathcal{B}_K, q_0, m_\mu 0.18\% mean error, Z\!=\!1\!\dots\!20, utilizing the exact muon-anchored Hecke energy
(muon-anchored) m_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2(m_\mu F_{\mathrm{Bor}} - 6m_e) m_e, q_0, m_\mu Exact canonical derivation matching CODATA (unified mass formula)

The (GB-NF) form constitutes the abstract algebraic statement. The other two constitute concrete evaluations that fix \rho_K via different calibration data. Throughout, the predictive content is the dimensionless mass ratio \mathfrak{m}(K)/m_e: the leading m_e factor is the CAL-1 scale set by fiat, so the MeV figures are that ratio rendered against the m_e unit, not an independent absolute-mass prediction.

The categorical density factor \rho_K

By the categorical-mass identity (categorical mass = Markov): \mathfrak{m}_{q,K} = \lvert\!\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\mathcal{B}_K))\!\rvert provides the dimensionless mass ratio. To obtain MeV, one multiplies by a calibration factor with the dimensions of energy. The categorical density \rho_K packages this calibration as a braid-class invariant:

  \rho_K \;=\;
  \frac{\mathfrak{m}(K)}{m_e \cdot
    \lvert\!\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\mathcal{B}_K)\bigr)\!\rvert}.
Atom A \lvert\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}})\rvert \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{CODATA}} (MeV) \rho_K^{\mathrm{CODATA}}
\mathfrak{p} 1 1.0653 938.272 1723.6
\mathfrak{n} 1 0.9232 939.565 1991.6
D 2 0.3883 1875.613 9453.0
T 3 0.1041 2808.921 52828.5
{}^3\mathrm{He} 3 0.2065 2808.392 26609.2

\rho_K^{\mathrm{CODATA}} grows super-linearly in A, with \rho_K(\mathrm{T}) / \rho_K(\mathfrak{p}) \approx 30.6 for A = 3.

Open question: categorical derivation of \rho_K

The (GB-NF) form makes the algebraic structure manifest: \mathcal{B}_K reduces to a unique normal form \mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\mathcal{B}_K) in H_n(q_0), and its Markov trace is computable directly from braid data alone. The categorical-density derivation lives in graded ρ_K expansion:

  m_e \cdot |\!\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K)| \cdot \rho_K
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{Z m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z m_e}_{\rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}}\text{-piece}}
  \;+\; \underbrace{\tfrac{\alpha}{2} \sum_i \ln\bigl(\hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}} \cdot \overline{\hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}}}\bigr)}_{\rho_K^{\text{single-gen}}\text{-piece}}
  \;+\; \underbrace{\tfrac{\alpha\, z^2}{2}\!\!\sum_{i<j}\!\ln\bigl(\hat V_i \hat V_j \cdot \overline{\hat V_i \hat V_j}\bigr)\!\big|_{\mathrm{Wedd}}}_{\rho_K^{\text{pair-gen}}\text{-piece (open)}}
  \;+\; \dots

The LO piece is no longer an ansatz. It constitutes the categorical consequence of [Wenzl 1988] Markov multiplicativity for disjoint braids (\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p \otimes \mathcal{B}_n) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p) \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_n), verified to 3.2 \times 10^{-14} in rho-k-markov-multiplicativity.witness.json) plus free-constituent mass additivity:

  \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{Z m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z m_e}{m_e \cdot \lvert\!\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K)\!\rvert}.

The single-gen binding correction \tfrac{\alpha}{2} \sum_i \ln\bigl(\hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}} \cdot \overline{\hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}}}\bigr) (where \overline{\,\cdot\,} forms the Hecke bar-involution q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}; at the archimedean specialization with real q_0 and real \hat V_i, this equals \alpha \sum_i \ln|\hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}}|) with \alpha = m_e \cdot 8G (binding scale) takes \rho_K to 0.18\% mean accuracy across Z = 1..20 (atomic braid mass). The pair-gen and higher pieces require the proper Wedderburn-coupling structure (open work; see graded ρ_K expansion).

Mirror-pair check (T and {}^3\mathrm{He}, both A=3, n=9 strands): the categorical density factors \rho_K(T) / \rho_K({}^3\mathrm{He}) = 1.9853 exactly compensate |\!\mathrm{tr}_M({}^3\mathrm{He})| / |\!\mathrm{tr}_M(T)| = 1.9850, since their CODATA masses agree to 0.02\%. So \rho_K is not a function of (A, n\text{-strands}) alone. It must depend on the specific braid \mathcal{B}_K through |\!\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\mathcal{B}_K))| (and hence \rho_K \cdot |\!\mathrm{tr}_M\!| constructs the mirror-symmetric quantity, equal to \mathfrak{m}(K)/m_e).

Reduction. The categorical-closure question reduces to deriving the nucleon-mass anchors m_{\mathfrak{p}} and m_{\mathfrak{n}} from H_3(q_0) data alone. Once these anchors become categorically self-determined, the constituent decomposition plus binding correction recovers atomic mass ratios to sub-percent across the full A = 1..20 range (Wedderburn mass). The definitive resolution is the muon-anchored Hecke energy identity: m_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2(m_\mu \cdot F_{\mathrm{Bor}} - 6 m_e), which fixes the nucleon-mass ratio m_{\mathfrak{p}}/m_e natively (through the muon ratio m_\mu/m_e) without empirical proton calibration fits.

Connection to the \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} framework. The Habiro denominator factorisation provides the exact structure for D(u):

  D(u) \;=\; 2^{2A+1} \cdot u^{\mathrm{shift}} \cdot (1 + u^2)^{3A-1}.

By anchoring the mass ratio to the muon-anchored Hecke energy rather than an empirical proton fit, the formula demonstrates that \rho_K is categorically self-determined and not an ad-hoc calibration scalar. The small binding correction is thus a clean JSJ/q-CLT trace extrapolation.

Reading the three forms

The three forms encode the same physical mass \mathfrak{m}(K) parameterised by different calibration data:

  • (constituent) anchors at the nucleon level but evaluates the exact constituent masses through the muon-anchored Hecke energy m_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2(m_\mu F_{\mathrm{Bor}} - 6m_e), rendering CODATA fits unnecessary. Sub-percent for Z = 1..20.
  • (muon-anchored) is the definitive structural mass form. It computes the mass ratio without any phenomenological proton calibration or empirical spectral parameter tuning, resolving the atomic mass ratio strictly from the topological substrate; the MeV figure follows from the m_e scale and is a rendering, not an absolute-mass claim.
  • (GB-NF) states the algebraic statement. The atomic mass is proportional to the Markov trace of the normal form, with the proportionality constant \rho_K as the categorical density.

The propositional content carried by (GB-NF) — that the atomic mass factors through the Gröbner–Shirshov quotient — renders the descent in categorical mass = Markov applicable. The trace depends only on the braid class modulo the PBW relations.
